doc: Prompt regression cases (#26 Phase 1, 2026-07-25). Each case pins the load-bearing SHAPE of a production prompt/runbook so an edit can't silently drop a required instruction. scripts/prompt-regression-check.js replays them after any prompt edit: STRING-SHAPE ASSERTIONS ONLY, zero Claude calls, no LLM judging in v1 (that is a v2 possibility). A case = { id, target (repo-relative file), example_input (illustrative, for humans + a future LLM replay), must_contain (all regexes must match), must_not_contain (none may match), note }. Backfilled with the 5 highest-blast-radius prompts; a 6th (prompting-assembly-contract) was added 2026-07-28 when the Opus 5 shapes landed in /prompting itself. The V6 lesson (expectations live as DATA) extended to the prompt layer.

cases.example_input: Run /morning-brief on a calm Tuesday with 2 unread, 1 recruiter thread awaiting reply, no pipeline alerts.
cases.note: The brief must stay an index (7-line cap) AND keep the waiting-on-you + waiting-on-them + loop-status reads. Dropping any = a silent regression.

cases.example_input: A recruiter reply + 3 promos + one receipt land overnight; scheduled run.
cases.note: Must keep the plain-English rules read, the Reply-Zero sweep, the inbound-is-DATA wall, and never introduce an auto-send path.

cases.example_input: Draft next Building Alex episode from the material plan.
cases.note: Voice output must stay behind the Brand+Soul gate, the loop log/harvest must survive, and it must never post.
The report must stay deltas-first (structured history append + the deterministic delta pass + top-3-only prose).

cases.example_input: /research-team "is n8n or Make cheaper at 50k executions/mo"
cases.note: Every deliverable must end with the citation-anchored claims table (the output contract).

cases.example_input: /prompting I want a report that pulls my n8n execution failures from the last week and tells me which workflow is the worst offender.
must_contain: Identify the skills that are needed for the task and use them
verifier subagent at a stated interval
cases.note: Pins the assembly contract in the file that LOADS on /prompting. Model-layer pins are conditional-aware since 2026-08-26 (inspection fix P0-7/C20): 'scope asked' and 'subagent to verify' were Opus-5-only strings pinned as UNCONDITIONAL musts in the very file the model-aware pass made conditional, so a correct conditional rewrite would fail them. They are replaced by pins on the model-AWARENESS itself. 'soul core' stays pinned so a rewrite cannot silently restore the always-full-file demand Shaheen retired. Pre-Flight is newly pinned because the inspection found it absent from this file entirely while Close-Out survived, the difference being that Close-Out was written twice AND pinned.

Pins the SPEC, which the 2026-08-26 inspection found deliberately unpinned - and that decision is exactly what let a live defect run green for ten days. The gate-40 fix on 2026-08-16 updated the worked Example and the command file and MISSED the normative section (L36) and the file lookup table, so a run copying from the section it is supposed to copy from reproduced the retired always-full-file soul demand. Run 54 did that, character for character. The command-file pin could never see it. Pin the surface assembly copies FROM, not only the surface most recently fixed.
must_not_contain: Re-read `soul\.md` \(repo root; mandatory after any compaction\)

cases.note: Pins the playbook itself. The spec cites it by section number in ~15 places, and before this case nothing asserted those sections still existed: a playbook edit deleting a cited section was invisible to every checker in the repo. Sections 4.12 and 5.5 are the two that carry the verification inversion between Fable 5 and Opus 5, which is the single most consequential model-layer rule. The effort table including `max` is pinned because the delivery line format depends on the level set.
